high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Balinese narrative illustration built as a terraced subak landscape: one farmer lifts a single gate in a fixed three-way irrigation divider, water enters only that existing channel, and the two closed channels remain dry beside an overflow basin, expressing deterministic routing without labels, arrows or diagram panels.

compositional_deconstruction.background: Steep Balinese rice terraces descend from a forested volcanic ridge beneath a pale eggshell sky. One spring-fed canal reaches a three-way stone divider at mid-height; clear water fills the left branch and its lower terrace, while the center and right branches remain dry. A shallow overflow basin sits below the divider. Flat earth red, leaf green, indigo, black and cream shapes define the landscape without photographic depth, written signs, screens, books, tablets, textile panels, arrows or sacred figures.

elements.desc: Stone-and-bamboo subak diversion weir spanning the central canal, built with exactly three permanent channel mouths and a lower overflow basin. The left bamboo sluice stands raised; the center and right sluices remain seated in their grooves. Each route is physically fixed in the masonry, with no movable pipe, new trench, written marker, arrow, control screen or decorative information panel.

Adult Balinese rice farmer operating the left sluice, medium brown skin, black hair wrapped in a plain indigo headcloth, rust-red long-sleeved shirt, cream sarong and bare feet. Kneeling beside the divider with a focused neutral expression, both hands lift one bamboo board while leaving the other gates untouched; no crown, badge, weapon, command staff or elevated seat appears.

Two adult Balinese farmers working together in the irrigated lower-left terrace, medium brown skin, black hair, plain leaf-green and ochre garments with indigo waist cloths. One guides the arriving water around young rice plants with a wooden hoe while the other steadies a seedling bundle; both remain level with the field rather than supervising the upstream operator.

Two closed field channels descending toward the center and right terraces, each edged by dark volcanic stones and ending before dry patterned mud. Their bamboo sluices remain visibly seated at the common divider and no water crosses their beds. The channels contain no hidden branch, glowing effect, written destination, symbolic flag, arrow, rope connector or human figure.
